input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: The guard uses all(...) instead of any(...) over the arguments' help attributes, so the section is gated on every argument being documented rather than on at least one.
- failure path: A command with arguments SRC (help set) and DST (no help) prints no 'Positional arguments' section at all in --help, silently dropping the documented text; conversely a command with zero arguments satisfies all([]) and prints an empty 'Positional arguments' header on every --help.

Reviewer finding
- description: When there are no Argument parameters, all() over an empty list is True, so an empty 'Positional arguments' heading is written for commands that take no positional arguments.
- rationale: Trigger: any command with only options and no arguments. The condition passes, and formatter.section emits the heading even though write_dl receives no rows. Impact: help output shows a spurious empty section on many commands.
critique: The finding identifies the all() guard and the all([]) == True case, which prints an empty 'Positional arguments' header. That is one of the labeled failure paths, caused by the same faulty all-vs-any guard. It leaves out the partially-documented case, but the faulty operation and mechanism are the same.
